objective: Expand AXIGNAL from the admitted European procurement wedge through a federated programme of official jurisdiction-specific procurement sources, adapters, taxonomies and commercial entitlements.
outcome: At least one non-TED official source progresses from catalogue to bounded technical probe, independent product admission, canonical lifecycle fidelity and jurisdiction-selective commercial availability without unsupported global claims or semantic flattening.

skills.activation_reason: Evaluate every official portal, API, feed or dataset independently across all rights dimensions.
Implement bounded source-specific adapters rather than a universal scraper.
Extend the canonical procurement model while preserving jurisdiction and lifecycle semantics.
Measure completeness, identifier stability, lifecycle depth, drift, freshness and outages.
Preserve original language, terminology, transliteration and translation provenance.
Profile public-contact, supplier and other personal-data exposure by jurisdiction.
Review credentials, rate limits, hostile documents, revocation and connector isolation.
Keep catalogue, technical probe, product admission and commercial availability as separate states.

external: Official source documentation and rights evidence
Qualified customer demand for a non-European jurisdiction
Approved jurisdiction-specific legal and privacy review

allowed_scope: Bounded technical probes with no public availability claim
Official API, OCDS, OData, bulk and feed adapters
Reversible CPV, NAICS, PSC, UNSPSC and native-taxonomy crosswalks
Lifecycle, award, contract and document fidelity tests
prohibited_scope: Global ingestion before European E2E and paid-value gates
One universal adapter that drops source semantics
Product support claim based only on catalogue listing
Country-wide support inferred from one federal or national source

acceptance_evidence.description: The v0.2 catalogue records 146 source families across 140 jurisdiction and government-level scopes, split into eight regional inventories and a versioned implementation queue.

Deterministic validation proves catalogue counts, unique identities, HTTPS or explicit feasibility boundaries, TED-only P0, SAM.gov first post-TED priority, NOCOPO long-tail placement and zero source admission.
The selected non-TED source has accepted collection, storage, model-input, transformation, display, export, redistribution, attribution and revocation records.
Bounded connector, parser, normaliser, taxonomy, lifecycle, outage, replay and rollback tests pass for the exact source profile.
Coverage, completeness, freshness, document availability, identifier stability, cost and crosswalk fidelity meet a predeclared source profile.
Qualified customers demonstrate recurring demand for the selected jurisdiction pack and understand its actual coverage boundary.
A paying organisation or approved equivalent commercial commitment validates the jurisdiction expansion value and cost.

traces: native object to canonical procurement model

rollback.strategy: Disable the affected source and jurisdiction entitlement, quarantine dependent claims and dossiers, preserve source-native evidence and audit history, and leave other jurisdiction packs operational.
rollback.kill_switch: Every source and jurisdiction pack must be independently revocable without a full deployment.

goal_lock_checks.evidence: The programme advances global discovery through official public-procurement systems.
Every canonical object and claim remains linked to source-native evidence and admission.
Jurisdictions share the InvestigationContext while preserving distinct semantics.
Customer demand prioritises research but cannot create source truth.
Original language and native taxonomies remain recoverable and versioned.
A source-specific global lifecycle and evidence graph is a defensible product asset.
Jurisdiction packs remain research tools rather than bid execution or guaranteed-outcome systems.
Rights, privacy, security, regulation and epistemic fidelity are critical gates.
Independent source and pack kill switches enable bounded rollback.
The task is blocked until the European E2E and paid-value dependencies pass.
